function: Channel estimation: a CNN refines the least-squares channel estimate of multi-user XL-MIMO, for near-field and far-field users, then is pruned and quantized (p. 3).
system: TDD multi-user XL-MIMO: BS ULA with M = 256 antennas, half-wavelength spacing, single-antenna users; no RIS; wavelength 0.01 m, 30 GHz band (pp. 2, 4).
method: 2D-CNN (nine zero-padded conv layers, residual denoising) trained supervised with MSE loss; then magnitude weight pruning with fine-tuning and post-training quantization (pp. 3-4).
data_channel: Synthetic hybrid-field (far plus near-field) steering-vector model of [8] with i.i.d. Gaussian path gains; 90,000 training, 10,000 validation, 2,000 test samples (p. 5).
test_conditions: Train: hybrid-field, L = 6 paths, one far-field. Test: pure near-field or far-field, L = 3 and 6, SNR -10 to 20 dB (p. 5).
baselines: Classical: LS, LMMSE, HOMP [8]. Learned: V-MRDN, a variant of the multiple residual dense network of [15] (p. 5).
metrics: NMSE versus SNR and versus quantization bit-width; number of weights; inference run time in ms (pp. 4-6).
complexity: FLOPs order O(M Nw), reduced by 1/(1-kappa) after pruning (p. 4); Table I: 263K to 29K weights, run time 0.2 to 0.078 ms (p. 6).
q1_support: p. 3: "generated by the hybrid-field channel model [8]". Custom steering-vector simulator with i.i.d. Gaussian path gains (page 2, Eq. 3); no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 5: "when facing with different numbers of paths". XLCNet trained once (L = 6, one far-field path) is tested on pure near-field and pure far-field channels with L = 3 and 6, without retraining.
q3_support: p. 5: "multiple residual dense network [15]". NMSE comparison against non-learned LS, LMMSE, HOMP and against the learned V-MRDN (Figs. 3 and 4, page 5: XLCNet outperforms the baselines).
q4_support: p. 6: "Run time (ms)". Table I lists weights (263K to 29K) and run time (0.2 to 0.078 ms); page 4 gives the FLOPs complexity order O(M Nw) of XLCNet and of the compressed model.
q5_support: p. 5: "based on the hybrid-field channel model in (9)". Data are self-generated by the paper's own simulator; no code or data link or DOI appears in the six pages, and no public dataset is used.
notes: PDF is the arXiv version (arXiv:2402.08916v1) and carries no DOI, so the DOI-title match cannot be checked from the PDF; title and content fit an IEEE TVT 2024 letter on XL-MIMO channel estimation. q2 is judged on the single XLCNet trained at L = 6 and tested at other L and on pure near-field or far-field channels (p. 5); the match-training curves retrain per condition and were not counted. q3: V-MRDN is a variant that the authors adapted from the published network of [15] (RIS cascaded-channel estimation), so the reviewer may confirm that it qualifies as the earlier learned baseline. Compression by pruning and quantization is an extra contribution to the channel estimation.
